summary_html: Reports via **state hotlines** (anonymous or confidential). CAPTA conditions funding on operating intake systems with confidentiality and good-faith protections.

key_cases.case_name: Clark County Department of Family Services v. Eighth Judicial District Court (Sharp)
key_cases.holding: NRS 432B.290(4) creates only a limited privilege for the identity of a person who reports suspected child abuse — available when the agency determines disclosure would harm an investigation or endanger a person — and it did not bar the court from ordering DFS to disclose reporter identities to a criminal defendant.
key_cases.relevance: The most recent Nevada authority on hotline-reporter confidentiality under NRS 432B.290(4).
key_cases.quote: we hold that the district court did not exceed its jurisdiction when it ordered DFS to release the names of the individuals who made the reports at issue

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: Officials may not enter a home or seize a child without prior judicial authorization unless they possess information at the time of seizure establishing reasonable cause to believe the child is in imminent danger of serious bodily injury, and the intrusion must be no broader than necessary to avert that injury.
key_cases.relevance: A hotline allegation, standing alone, does not supply the reasonable cause required for warrantless entry or seizure.
key_cases.quote: reasonable cause to believe that the child is in imminent danger of serious bodily injury and that the scope of the intrusion is reasonably necessary to avert that specific injury.

key_cases.case_name: In re Parental Rights as to J.D.N.
key_cases.holding: The juvenile 'J' file does not automatically form part of the family division's record in a termination proceeding and is admissible only if it satisfies Nevada's evidence rules, including the hearsay rule; NRS 128.090(3) removes only privilege objections, not hearsay objections. A parent who objects to the entire file without identifying the specific hearsay portions waives the objection. Once an NRS 128.109 presumption applies, the parent may rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence. Affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Hotline intake documents in the 'J' file are admissible only through a hearsay rule or exception, not by virtue of being in the agency's file.
key_cases.quote: the "J" file is only admissible if it complies with Nevada's statutes and rules of evidence, including the hearsay rule and any hearsay exception

mandatory_reporters: Designated professionals only (not universal) — NRS 432B.220(1) and (4); any other person may make a report but is not required to (NRS 432B.220(5))

A person providing services licensed or certified in this State pursuant to, without limitation, NRS chapters 450B, 630, 630A, 631, 632, 633, 634, 634A, 634B, 635, 636, 637, 637B, 639, 640, 640A, 640B, 640C, 640D, 640E, 641, 641A, 641B, 641C, 641D or 653, or practicing as an emergency medical technician, advanced emergency medical technician or paramedic in this State under the Recognition of Emergency Medical Services Personnel Licensure Interstate Compact ratified by NRS 450B.145 — NRS 432B.220(4)(a)

Any personnel of a medical facility licensed pursuant to NRS chapter 449 who are engaged in the admission, examination, care or treatment of persons, or an administrator, manager or other person in charge of such a medical facility upon notification of suspected abuse or neglect of a child by a member of the staff of the medical facility — NRS 432B.220(4)(b)
Members of the clergy, practitioners of Christian Science and religious healers, unless the knowledge was acquired from the offender during a confession — NRS 432B.220(4)(d)
Persons employed by a public or private school and persons who serve as volunteers at such a school — NRS 432B.220(4)(e)

Any person who maintains or is employed by a facility or establishment that provides care for children, a children's camp or any other public or private facility, institution or agency furnishing care to a child — NRS 432B.220(4)(f)
Persons licensed under NRS chapter 424 to conduct a foster home — NRS 432B.220(4)(g)
Officers and employees of a law enforcement agency and adult or juvenile probation officers — NRS 432B.220(4)(h)
Attorneys, except as otherwise provided in NRS 432B.225 — NRS 432B.220(4)(i)

Any person who maintains, is employed by or serves as a volunteer for an agency or service which advises persons regarding the abuse or neglect of a child and refers them for help — NRS 432B.220(4)(j)
Persons employed by or serving as volunteers for a youth shelter — NRS 432B.220(4)(k)
Any adult employed by an entity that provides organized activities for children, including a school district or public school — NRS 432B.220(4)(l)
Persons enrolled with Medicaid to provide doula services — NRS 432B.220(4)(m)
Certified prevention specialists, peer recovery support specialists and peer recovery support specialist supervisors — NRS 432B.220(4)(n)

Reports must be made to an agency which provides child welfare services or to a law enforcement agency as soon as reasonably practicable and not later than 24 hours after the reporter knows or has reasonable cause to believe a child has been abused or neglected — NRS 432B.220(1)

timeline_requirements.deadline: An investigation must be initiated immediately if the report indicates that there is a high risk of serious harm to the child, that the child has suffered a fatality, or that the child is living in a household in which another child has died, or the child is seriously injured or has visible signs of physical abuse (NRS 432B.260(2)); otherwise the agency which provides child welfare services must conduct an evaluation not later than 3 days after the report or notification was received to determine whether an investigation is warranted (NRS 432B.260(3)) and, if it is, must initiate the investigation not later than 3 days after the evaluation is completed (NRS 432B.260(4))
timeline_requirements.starts_from: A report concerning the possible abuse or neglect of a child is received by an agency which provides child welfare services or by a law enforcement agency, or the child welfare agency is notified by a law enforcement agency that it has received such a report (NRS 432B.260(2) and (3))
